title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of heat-treated cold spray additively manufactured titanium metal matrix composites
InformationInFigures: Yes. Rockwell B Hardness values in Fig. 7

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Heat_Treatment_Description: dried in a vacuum oven for 16 h at 80°C
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: roughening via grit blasting and then cleaning with ethanol

experimentalProperties.Spraying_System_Model: PCS 1000 L, Plasma Giken Co. Ltd., Saitama, Japan
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: Chemical analysis was performed by cutting specimens into small pieces and weighing, then a solution of g 2 ml of 69 % nitric acid, 4 ml of 37 % hydrochloric acid, and 1 ml of 48 % hydrofluoric acid was used to react. After the reaction was complete, solutions were made to volume with Milli-Q DI water and analysed. Selected as-sprayed and heat-treated cold-sprayed rectangular blocks were sliced, set in epoxy, ground, and polished for metallographic analysis. Tensile tests were cylinders

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: no change to the phase composition of feedstock, deposit was entirely α-Ti. porous microstructure with no apparent cracks. Most splats maintain their initial spherical shapes, indicating limited plastic deformation during impact.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Final concentration of deposit was 3.5 wt% YSZ and 96.5 wt% Ti. reduced ZrO2 content and a phase change from monoclinic ZrO2 to cubic ZrO2, and elevated lattice parameters due to thermal expansion. a dense microstructure with secondary (reinforcement) particles distributed uniformly throughout the CP Ti matrix was achieved. there was sintering inside and between initially sprayed particles & secondary particle fragments, this diffusing the inter-splat boundaries and the recrystallization of metal grains.
